en: The Attainment of the Knowledge of Reality.
Om, homage to the venerable lady Vajravārāhī!
This Fortune of the Fully Enlightened One has arrived from her adornment of the ocean of bliss;
she is endowed with all forms of excellence and destroys the mass of darkness that is the world's evil.
She is the steadfastness of the treasury of the knowledge of light, the tranquility of the treasury of mindfulness, and the wisdom of the treasury of insight.
May the Blessed Lady Vajravirāsinī protect the three worlds from misfortune.
Having paid homage to the pollen of the lotus feet of the illustrious Vajradevī and to the state of the Guru, [I shall explain] the illustrious Saṃvara,
the concealed bodhicitta.
The state of non-duality between wisdom and compassion is praised.
By the monk Jñānandra, whose name is Candreśvaraśarman, who abides in the bliss of prostrating at the pair of feet of Vajradevī.
A brief exposition of the *sādhana* of Vajravārāhī for one’s own benefit is here set forth;
my mind is ever eager for conceptualization toward the bestower of eloquent speech. (Tjs 0.4)
Therefore, this has been composed by me with faith and with a dull and limited intellect;
great people should not look for faults in me.
Oṃ, homage to Śrī Vajravārāhī!
Arisen from the wheel of the soles, flickering like a flash of lightning,
she has incinerated the three realms of existence, is honored by the three worlds, and is drenched in a stream of nectar.

May Vārāhī protect you— she who is permeated by the essence of the Buddha’s wisdom, free from turbidity, bestowing a mass of her own bliss, and devoid of the conceptualization of existence and non-existence.
Situated within the solar mandala of the emanation lotus, encircled by the letters beginning with *ka* and the rest,
blazing with the fire of kindled flames and drinking the nectar of immortality— subtle as a fine thread, she is the Vidyā who consumes the assembly of Buddhas, piercing through the three wheels.
May Vārāhikā, joyful and moving with graceful gait, manifest within your hearts.
Having prostrated with my head before Vajravārāhī, the Vajrayoginī who is preceded by the Vajra,
I shall speak for the sake of my own recollection the complete accomplishment of the knowledge of reality.
The wise one, mindful and with his body held straight, should enter a secluded and favorable place;
there, having sat upon a soft seat, he should contemplate purification.
Thereafter, having written the heart-mantra of Vajradhara with the sixth syllable recited three times using the ring finger,
one should honor it with red flowers.
Thereafter, having placed the lotus-hand in the left [hand] upon the vessel of Paramādya,
one should perform the libation according to the instruction by touching the [left] shoulder.
Having performed the *karanyāsa* by joining the thumbs and fingers together,
one should perform the *aṅganyāsa* with the six mantras of Vīreśvarī.
Thereafter, upon the excellent wheel-vajra, one should slowly sprinkle the mantra born of the union with the dawn-red pigment,
using highly distinguished powders derived from serpents placed within a cloth.
There, having carefully drawn the wheel of the Victor’s heart with a hundred million peacock feathers,
one should inscribe the garland of mantras within its center using a probe made of gold from the Ganges.
On the outer circumference of the wheel, in the directions of the east, north, west, and south,
one should draw six svastikas in sequence with the left hand.
Having drawn forth the Vajra Goddess, entered [her], and bound her within the syllables of the mantra,
one should satisfy her by reciting "jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ" according to the proper ritual procedure.
Thereafter, one should perform various forms of worship for her who exists in the form of mantra,
with foods to be chewed, swallowed, licked, drunk, and sucked, possessing all desirable qualities.

With various offerings accompanied by intoxication, with the five most excellent types of oblations, and with songs, instrumental music, dances, circumambulations, prostrations, and hymns of praise; Tjs_1.13 //
Desiring its accomplishment, one should perform the prescribed ritual of worship on the tenth lunar day, either daily, every fortnight, or every month. (Tjs 1.14)
Then, having performed the ritual of external worship, the one of vast compassion [sat] upon the lotus of his enemy’s heart which he had fashioned.
One should meditate upon the goddess previously described, who possesses a body as radiant as the orb of the sun and is free from all enemies.
She has the color of vermilion at twilight, surpassing the luster of seven suns with her mass of rays;
she holds in her right hand a curved knife that destroys all suffering and radiates the light of nectar.
She holds in her left hand an exceedingly white lotus, and [her right] is adorned with a banner filled with blood;
her head is encircled by Kālī, who wields a thunderbolt, and her hair is loose with hands raised above.
Her body is adorned with a garland of severed heads; blood flows from her mouth as she tastes it while uttering a loud roar.
With one face turned upward to the left, she possesses an excellent and auspicious gait, yet her primary face is characterized by wrath.
Full of bliss and passion, endowed with various aesthetic sentiments, she dances in the half-lotus posture.
Her limbs were sealed by the six mudrās; she was sixteen years of age, possessed of excellent form, and divested of clothing.
Having performed the ritual procedures for summoning knowledge and so forth as before, the mantra-knower,
skilled in the rites, should meditate on a single swastika revolving rapidly and facing toward his own forehead.
Thereafter, in the element of space, within the cavern of Mount Trikūṭa, one should meditate upon the previously described wheel as it revolves, red in color and intensely blazing.
There, blazing like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker due to its extreme steadiness,
it melts the great wheel of bliss, performing a libation with the essence of flowing nectar.

One should subsequently perceive that which has the nature of the three bodies, which is supreme, innate, and pervades the world, a continuous stream of radiating infinite peace; afterwards, there is bliss.
One should contemplate this every day, at every twilight, or whenever there is leisure; it is clearly stated that this should continue until the signs of accomplishment appear. Tjs 2.7.
When this [state] has been clearly cultivated through the continuous connection with joy and absorption that arise without effort, [then it is attained].
If there is no pain from whips, slaps, and the like here, then accomplishment will be near at hand.
If the sharp sound of beaten drums and other instruments is not within the range of hearing,
then the unsurpassed, supreme enlightenment is attained, just as the foremost accomplishment of one who meditates for a long time is realized even in a dream.
Having perceived the signs of accomplishment in a cemetery, a mountain thicket, at the foot of a tree, or similar locations,
the wise one, dwelling there, should constantly practice the yoga of the generation stage.
Upon the accomplishment [of this], the earth and the other elements indeed undergo dissolution in successive order;
at that time, there arises the reality which is consciousness-only, luminous and resembling the sky.
One should recognize them by their signs; those who know it understand the signs to be fivefold.
Therefore, a yogi, being composed in meditation, should perceive them with the mind.
First, the sign appears like a mirage; the second sign has the form of smoke;
the third is like fireflies; and the fourth is clearly a blazing lamp.
The fifth sign is like a cloudless sky—luminous and free from conceptual construction;
having thus attained the sign, one obtains the great mudrā.

Desiring to rise, the knower of yoga, having prostrated to the Yoginī and the Lord, and having uttered "mūḥ" while remaining composed, should rise and perform his duties; possessing true wisdom, he should always remain joined in the yoke of yoga.
Thus ends the rule for meditative cultivation (bhāvanā) for the sake of attaining the knowledge of reality. // 2 //
And he was repeatedly entreated by his disciples, who had formed circles with their hands joined at their hearts before his lotus-like feet.
On the tenth lunar day, the minister should bestow his grace upon them.
Having worshipped the Goddess in the form of the mantra residing within the wheel, and having performed the yoga,
one should take up the supreme primordial mantra recited with mantras and emerge from that [mandala].
Then the Guru should behold the disciple, who has performed the five circumambulations, standing at the southern side of the mandala, holding a garland of flowers, and meditating upon the Lord.
Thereafter, having meditated upon the aforementioned circle of goddesses as rapidly emerging with radiating rays,
one should bestow [the empowerment] of the Vajra-holder upon his body, which is situated within.
Thus there may be possession, its bud-like stage, trembling, tears, falling [into a swoon], the arising of knowledge, and even one's own true nature; these are to be brought to fulfillment.
Thereafter, one should explain the meditative absorption (samādhi) and the mantra of Vajrayoginī to one who is endowed with faith,
possesses virtuous qualities, and has true devotion that does not distinguish between the guru and the Buddha.
One should not speak of this yoga, which produces immediate conviction and is well-accomplished.
For a disciple whose mind is devoid of faith and who is bereft of devotion.
But for one who performs worship of the circle of goddesses conjoined with the mantra,
the eight fears and the great evils depart from him.
Misfortune, poverty, disease, old age, suffering, and dejection;
delusion, strife, turbid afflictions, and manifold torments as well.
He who recites the wheel-mantra while meditating on it within his heart with speech restrained attains the eight siddhis, as well as the five superknowledges and the eight qualities.
He who meditates with effort every day at the four junctions of the day upon her whose face is radiant as the sun conquers death, which cannot be overcome even by Hari, Hara, and Hiraṇyagarbha.

For him who meditates upon the Aśanikolamukhī together with her wheel, there arise vast lands of clothing, food, drink, wealth, and grain; celestial palaces, divine beds, seats, and requisites; beloved women; and various branches of knowledge. 12.
Thus concludes the procedure for favoring disciples, together with its benefits, for the sake of the perfect attainment of the knowledge of reality.
Henceforth, I shall set forth the extraction of the mantra, the heart of Vajrayoginī,
which has been transmitted from ear to ear and from mouth to mouth in due succession.
Having drawn the wheel as previously described, provided with the abodes of the hosts of Maruts,
one should there, following the sequence, write the vowels and consonants (ālikāli) in the same manner in the corners.

Having first written the triad consisting of the letter *ja* with *dha* below, the letter *ḍa* with *ra* below, and adorned with the letter *ha* with *dha* below— this six-syllable mantra illuminates reality.
The letter *bh* joined with the upper [letter] and combined with the one situated above it is to be written as the one situated above;
then, the letter *ḍ* joined with the lower [letter], resting upon *ṣ*, and combined with the one situated above *ṣ* and the one situated above it.
[The seed-syllable] joined with ña and situated below ra, then situated above pa and joined with ṭa;
thereafter, joined with pha and situated above tha which is accompanied by ṭha, and joined with ai and va, situated at the end of ha. Tjs 4.5.
[The letter] *ca* situated in the middle of the *sa*, joined with the *tha* on its right, well-established below the *bha*;
thereafter [the letter] *ha* situated in the middle of the *tha*, joined with the *ta* on its left, and finally [the letter] situated in the middle of the *ṭha* and *la*.

The final letter of the entire [consonant] series, joined with the first letter of the third group situated to its left; joined above with the letter *ṇa*, with the letter *la* below it, and the letter *cha* situated above; and joined to the right with the letter *ṭha*.
The letter *t* with its upper part joined to the lower *ṣ*; the lower *th* joined to the upper *da*; then the lower *ṇ* joined to the lower *pa*;
the lower *pha* joined to the lower *ṭha*; the *ph* situated above, joined to the upper *ṇ*; and the lower *la*.
Accompanied by the lower *ḍa* and the void (*śūnya*), situated above the three folds and resting on the *ra*-vowel;
joined with the lower *tha*, situated upon the lower *śa*, and likewise conjoined with the lower *ña*.
This secret mantra of the goddess Aśanīdevī, composed of the syllables *sa*, *ya*, *ma*, *dha*, *ga*, *ṃ*, *jha*, *vā*, *ma*, *ga*, and *sa*, should be written, recited, and meditated upon. Tjs_4.10.
The wish-fulfilling gem, the celestial tree, the supreme vessel, and even the auspicious cow of plenty are praised;
when propitiated, they bestow wealth here in this world, yet it is he who grants happiness along with true riches.
Thus ends the procedure for the extraction of mantras for the sake of the perfect accomplishment of the knowledge of reality.
Having inscribed this in a vessel according to the ritual,
one who knows the procedure should perform the protection of the child in accordance with the rules for the sake of worship.
The two necks, the crest, and the two arms are increased by one.
Upon seeing him, serpents flee along with their young, as do spirits, seizing demons, night-stalkers, and hosts of piśācas;
and other terrifying beings who cause fear and distress to children, like forest-dwelling beasts fleeing in terror from a powerful lion. // 2 //
Having received the authentic instruction and having gained conviction in yoga,
this accomplishment— whose very life-breath is radiant, stainless knowledge— has been fully inscribed.

Therefore, for the sake of attaining that [state], one should serve the lotus feet of the Guru with food offerings, according to the rules of giving, through physical austerities, and by prostrations. // 4 //

By whatever stainless merit, as pure as the rays of the full moon, may have been produced by me through this work— which, like the attainment of the supreme knowledge of reality, brings great benefit to people in this world—
may all beings in the world become pure, free from the stains of the Kali age, and partakers of perfect enlightenment.
Having obtained the noble mudrā, which pacifies the fear of existence and accomplishes the welfare of all sentient beings. // 5 //
This concludes the Svādhiṣṭhāna, titled "The Perfection of the Knowledge of Reality"; may it be auspicious forever.
